title: VPC-isolated upgrade orchestration, image signing, and egress policy requirements
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Problem: Customers running Redwood Private in isolated VPCs or air-restricted networks need a clearly defined, auditable upgrade process that works without outbound internet access, preserves network egress controls, and enforces signed artifacts. Current docs and acceptance criteria are fragmented across prior tickets. This PRD consolidates requirements for: 1) an orchestrated upgrade path that supports pull-through registries and offline bundles; 2) mandatory image signing and verification at runtime and during upgrade; 3) network egress rules and a minimal outbound allowlist for control plane handshakes where required; and 4) rollback and maintenance-window semantics for restricted networks.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade orchestration: Customers can perform a staged upgrade (canary -> blue/green) entirely from within a VPC with no direct internet access by using either (a) a customer-provided pull-through registry or (b) a signed offline bundle delivered via secure transfer. Steps and exit conditions documented.

Bundle format: Offline upgrade bundles must be a single signed tarball with metadata.json that lists component versions, image digests, signing key ID, and deterministic install order. The runtime verifies signature before applying changes.

Image signing: All images and bundles used for Private must be signed using a recommended key format (PKCS#7 or similar). The installer and runtime perform signature verification against a keyset managed by the customer or by Redwood (customer choice). Verification failures abort the upgrade with clear error codes.

Egress allowlist: The product defines a minimal, well-documented set of endpoints and ports required for optional control-plane features (e.g., telemetry opt-in, license validation) and a documented mode where these are disabled. Customers running in locked-down mode may opt-out and use offline bundles instead.

Rollback and idempotence: Upgrades support automated rollback on health-check failures observed within the maintenance window. State migration steps must be idempotent and reversible where feasible; documentation lists non-reversible steps and required backups.
Upgrade observability: Console and on-prem CLI generate an upgrade plan preview and a post-upgrade report (version diffs, failed components, logs) that can be exported for audits.
Operator controls: Admins can schedule maintenance windows, force-fail a rollout, and promote canary to primary. All admin actions are recorded in audit logs with user, timestamp, and justification.

Compatibility matrix: The acceptance doc includes a matrix of supported OS/kernel versions, container runtimes, and CRI versions for offline upgrades; upgrades attempted outside the matrix produce a preflight warning blocking the operation.

Automated tests: Engineering provides an end-to-end test harness that validates an offline bundle upgrade in a simulated isolated VPC environment; the test must be included in the release pipeline and pass before GA.
Security review: Changes pass an internal security review and include threat modeling for supply-chain attacks, including recovery procedures for compromised signing keys.
Documentation & runbook: Public-facing install and upgrade docs updated; an internal runbook for support (troubleshooting steps, common failures, and escalation path) published before rollout.

Customer migration path: For customers currently on hosted-assisted upgrades, provide a documented migration checklist to move to strictly offline upgrades including required artifacts and steps to validate installation integrity.
notes: Decision: Prefer a single signed offline bundle format for air-restricted customers to reduce complexity; pull-through registries remain supported for hybrid setups.

Trade-off: Supporting both customer-managed keysets and Redwood-managed keysets increases implementation scope but significantly improves customer flexibility; key management integration will be gated by security review.
Constraint: We will not require customers to open arbitrary outbound ports; any required external endpoints must be minimal and optional for fully offline operation.
Related tickets: This consolidates acceptance criteria from prior PM tickets and is intended to be canonical for the next private release.
Implementation note: Runtime needs a compact verification module; engineering recommends reuse of existing signature libraries (cosign/notation) where license permits.
